title: A scalar vacuum shift cannot keep both the beta=1 Wick lower bound and free-vacuum expectation uniform

scalar_shift_tension.shifted_polynomial: For P_C+d, the exact lower bound is d-6C^2
scalar_shift_tension.vacuum_expectation: For a centered Gaussian X with variance C, E[P_C(X)]=0, so E[P_C(X)+d]=d
scalar_shift_tension.uniform_lower_bound_price: A lower bound at least -L independent of N requires d_N>=6C_N^2-L
scalar_shift_tension.covariance_growth: For beta=1 on three-dimensional torus cutoffs, C_N=sum_(|k|<=N)(2 sqrt(m^2+|k|^2))^(-1)=Theta(N^2)
scalar_shift_tension.vacuum_growth: Every scalar shift giving a cutoff-uniform lower bound therefore has free-vacuum expectation Omega(N^4)
scalar_shift_tension.zero_expectation_horn: Choosing d_N=0 keeps the free-vacuum expectation zero but leaves the exact lower bound -6C_N^2
scalar_shift_tension.ceiling: This is a scalar-shift tension, not a no-go for non-Gaussian measures, singular dressings, additional counterterms or renormalized resolvent limits
